title: The inclusions $\underline E\to\underline F$
statement:
Let $E\subseteq F$ be finite subextensions of $\Qlb/\mathbf Q_\ell$
([sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]), with the topologies restricted from $\Qlb$, and let
$\underline E$, $\underline F$ be their condensed rings
([def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring]). The morphism
$\iota_{E,F}\colon\underline E\to\underline F$ is postcomposition with the inclusion
$E\subseteq F$ ([def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]), viewed as a morphism of the
underlying ring objects of $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$. It is strictly functorial:
$\iota_{E,E}=\mathrm{id}$, and $\iota_{F,H}\circ\iota_{E,F}=\iota_{E,H}$ for
$E\subseteq F\subseteq H$.

proof.text: Write $j_{E,F}:E\hookrightarrow F$ for the field inclusion. The topology on each field is the subspace topology from $\Qlb$, as specified in [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring]. For an open $U\subseteq F$, write $U=F\cap V$ with $V$ open in $\Qlb$. Then $j_{E,F}^{-1}(U)=E\cap V$ is open in $E$, so $j_{E,F}$ is continuous. It preserves $0,1,+,\cdot$ because both fields have the operations induced from $\Qlb$; it is therefore a continuous ring homomorphism.

source.place: first sentence: continuity of the inclusion

proof.text: Apply [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map] to $j_{E,F}$. This defines $\iota_{E,F}$ as a morphism of condensed rings, and as a morphism of their underlying ring objects, with section map, for every profinite set $S$, $C(S,E)\to C(S,F)$ given by $a\mapsto j_{E,F}\circ a$. In particular it has exactly the source and target of the item. At each section it preserves the ring operations, and for $u:S'\to S$ the equality $(j_{E,F}\circ a)\circ u=j_{E,F}\circ(a\circ u)$ describes its naturality.

source.place: second sentence: application of the continuous-map construction

proof.text: The inclusions satisfy $j_{E,E}=\mathrm{id}_E$ and $j_{F,H}\circ j_{E,F}=j_{E,H}$ as functions, hence as continuous ring homomorphisms. The strict functoriality in [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map] consequently gives $\iota_{E,E}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\iota_{F,H}\circ\iota_{E,F}=\iota_{E,H}$. Explicitly, on every section $a:S\to E$ these equations are $j_{E,E}\circ a=a$ and $j_{F,H}\circ(j_{E,F}\circ a)=j_{E,H}\circ a$. Thus they are equalities of the specified morphisms, not merely isomorphisms between constructions.

source.place: third sentence: strict identity and composition laws

proof_origin.place: def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-map.proof.md, first–third sentences; elementary details expanded from the source proof
